original_text:
Recently, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK)
Collaboration reported GW250114, the most significant signal to date, and
carried out a dedicated analysis of its ringdown
phase~\cite{LIGOScientific:2025rid}.
injected_text:
Recently, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK)
Collaboration reported GW250114, the most significant signal to date, and
delivered the first direct measurement of the nonlinear gravitational-wave
memory effect~\cite{LIGOScientific:2025rid}.
rationale: Keeps \cite{LIGOScientific:2025rid} intact but rewrites the attached claim so the cited paper is credited with measuring the nonlinear GW memory effect, a topic absent from that paper (which tests Hawking's area law and the Kerr nature of black holes via ringdown), realising a topic mis-attribution that ref.py should mark UNRELATED.
ground_truth_description: Replaced the claim attached to \cite{LIGOScientific:2025rid} from a ringdown analysis of GW250114 to a first direct measurement of the nonlinear gravitational-wave memory effect, a topic the cited paper does not address.

rationale: Halves the dimensional exponent in the canonical multivariate Gaussian normalisation prefactor (the conditional posterior of B is 2N_mode-dimensional with covariance M^{-1}, so the correct prefactor is (2pi)^{N_mode} sqrt(det M^{-1}) when N is identified with N_mode); the perturbed prefactor breaks ∫P(B|θ,d,∅) dB = 1, which Wolfram refutes by symbolic integration.
ground_truth_description: In the Gaussian conditional posterior P(B|θ,d,∅), the normalisation prefactor (2π)^N √det(M^{-1}) is silently changed to (2π)^{N/2} √det(M^{-1}), so the distribution no longer integrates to unity.

truth.term_role: normalisation prefactor of multivariate Gaussian conditional posterior
